Trump names Sergio Gor as next US ambassador to India: Calls him key aide; senate confirmation awaited
item.description: Donald Trump announced Sergio Gor, the current director of the White House Presidential personnel office, as the next US ambassador to India and Special Envoy for South and Central Asian Affairs. Trump praised Gor as a trusted friend and someone capable of delivering on his agenda. Gor's confirmation by the Senate is pending, after which he will succeed Eric Garcetti.

item.title: US defence secretary fires DIA chief: General whose Iran strike assessment sparked Trump’s anger; military shake-up continuous
item.description: Lt General Jeffrey Kruse is out as DIA head. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth took the action. This followed President Donald Trump's unhappiness. The agency's Iran nuclear assessment caused the issue. The assessment differed from Trump's public statements. This dismissal is amid a broader shake-up. Several senior officials have also exited. Pentagon officials have not commented.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: ‘Make cities very, very safe’: Trump intensifies federal crackdown; says Chicago, New York next in line
item.description: Donald Trump announced intensified federal action against crime in Chicago and New York. This follows deployment of national guard personnel to Washington DC. Trump cited rising lawlessness as the reason. Local officials criticised the move as politically motivated. The administration argues federal intervention is necessary where local leadership is ineffective. Critics worry about politicising policing.

item.title: Cash in chips bag row: NYC mayor Adam’s ex-aide calls it 'birthday gift'; says ‘reporter tried to hurt me'
item.description: Winnie Greco, ex-advisor to New York City Mayor Eric Adams, claims a cash-filled potato chip bag given to journalist Katie Honan was a misunderstood birthday gift rooted in Chinese culture. Greco suggests Honan intended harm, a claim Honan denies. Greco's attorney insists the money was a kind gesture, not a bribe.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: NYC-bound tour bus crashes: Indian, asian tourists among victims; multiple fatalities reported
item.description: A tour bus, carrying mostly Indian, Chinese, and Filipino nationals, crashed in upstate New York on Friday, resulting in fatalities and injuries. The bus, en route to New York City from Niagara Falls, overturned near Pembroke for unknown reasons. Rescue operations are underway, with a child among the deceased. Many passengers were ejected or remain trapped.

item.title: Want power back? Democrats told to drop 45 'woke' words - list revealed
item.description: A Third Way memo urges Democrats to drop 45 "woke" terms, arguing they alienate voters and harm the party's chances. The think tank believes this language makes Democrats sound elitist and out of touch with everyday people. By adopting clearer, more accessible language, Democrats can broaden their appeal and improve their electability.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Treasury’s No 2 out: Michael Faulkender quits in 5 months; second top exit in a month
item.description: Michael Faulkender is stepping down as US Treasury Department's deputy secretary after less than five months in the role. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent praised Faulkender's contributions to the "One Big Beautiful Bill" and the "GENIUS Act," as well as his work on sanctions. His departure follows that of IRS chief Billy Long, marking recent leadership changes within the department.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Epstein files incoming: Hundreds of DOJ docs expected Friday; house panel eyes transparency
item.description: The House oversight committee is set to receive hundreds of DOJ documents related to the Epstein and Maxwell investigation, following a congressional subpoena. While Republicans push for transparency, concerns linger about potential implications for government agencies and individuals linked to Trump. A bipartisan effort is also underway to force a full House vote on releasing all Epstein-related documents.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: 'Ready to meet Zelenskyy': Sergey Lavrov sets Putin okay with meeting Ukrainian President - but with this condition
item.description: Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov stated that President Putin is open to meeting with Ukraine's Zelenskyy, provided that crucial conflict resolution matters are thoroughly addressed. This follows Trump's suggestion for a one-on-one meeting before a potential trilateral summit. Zelenskyy has expressed willingness to negotiate directly, though Lavrov claims he seeks a swift meeting for international attention, while avoiding serious negotiations.

item.title: 'Eliminating all retaliatory tariffs on US goods': Canada's big announcement; move comes day after Carney-Trump talks
item.description: Canada will eliminate tariffs on American goods covered by USMCA starting September 1. This follows a call between Prime Minister Mark Carney and US President Donald Trump. Both countries are intensifying discussions on a broader trade deal. Canada will retain tariffs on steel, aluminum, and autos. The USMCA is scheduled for review in 2026.
item.dc:creator: TOI Business Desk

item.title: Botswana secures historic $12 billion investment agreement from Qatar’s Al Mansour Holdings
item.description: Botswana has secured a $12 billion investment deal with Qatar’s Al Mansour Holdings, targeting sectors like infrastructure, mining, and cybersecurity. Amid economic contraction and declining diamond revenues, the ten-year agreement aims to drive diversification and long-term growth. Part of Qatar’s broader African strategy, the deal positions Botswana as a key regional partner in strategic development.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Security escalation: US defence secretary arms National Guard in DC; Trump warns of full federal takeover
item.description: The Pentagon has announced that National Guard troops deployed in Washington, D.C., for President Trump's law enforcement crackdown will now be armed, marking a significant escalation in security measures. Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth issued the order, while nearly 2,000 National Guard members remain stationed in the city. Trump declared D.C. is safe again, praising the National Guard and police.
